Samkhya.question: Though in conventional terms the bondage is ascribed to the _____ṣa, this is ultimately a mistake

Samkhya.fact: The cause under consideration here is Prakṛti or more precisely Moola-Prakṛti ("Primordial Matter"). In evolution, Prakṛti is transformed and differentiated into multiplicity of objects.

Samkhya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Samkhya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Samkhya.question: Another uniqueness of Sāmkhya is that not only physical entities but even mind, ego and intelligence are regarded as forms of _____, quite distinct from pure consciousness

Samkhya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Samkhya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Samkhya.question: In a state of equilibrium of three gunas, when the three together are one, "unmanifest" _____ṛti which is unknowable
Samkhya.fact: Samkhya theorizes that Prakṛti is the source of the perceived world of becoming. The evolution itself is possible because Prakṛti is always in a state of tension among its constituent strands or gunas – sattva, rajas and tamas.

Samkhya.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Samkhya.question: The evolution obeys causality relationships, with primal _____ itself being the material cause of all physical creation
Samkhya.fact: The evolution obeys causality relationships, with primal Nature itself being the material cause of all physical creation. Sita.fact: She gives birth to twin sons there: Kusha and Lava.

Sita.fact: Ravana's daughter: In Sanghadasa's Jaina version of Ramayana, and also in Adbhuta Ramayana, Sita, entitled Vasudevahindi, is born as the daughter of Ravana. According to this version, astrologers predict that the first child of Vidyadhara Maya (Ravana's wife) will destroy his lineage.

Sita.fact: During this time, Vishvamitra had brought Rama and his brother Lakshmana to the forest for the protection of a yajna (ritual sacrifice). Sita.fact: Hearing of the svayamvara, Vishvamitra asked Rama to participate in the ceremony with the consent of Janaka, who agreed to offer Sita's hand in marriage to the prince if he could fulfil the requisite task. Sita.fact: During the homeward journey to Ayodhya, another avatar of Vishnu, Parashurama, challenged Rama to combat, on the condition that he was able to string the bow of Vishnu, Sharanga. The wedding entourage then reached Ayodhya and they entered the city amid great fanfare.

Sita.fact: The values that she enshrined and adhered to at every point in the course of a demanding life are the values of womanly virtue held sacred by countless generations of Indians. Known for her feminine courage, she is often been cited as one of the defining figures of Indian womanhood.

Vallabha.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: The _____ was One of the six orthodox traditions of Hindu philosophy.
Vedanta.fact: Vedanta (; Sanskrit: वेदान्त, IAST: Vedānta [ʋeːdɑ́ːntɐ]), also called Uttara Mīmāṃsā, is one of the six orthodox (āstika) schools of Hindu philosophy and textual exegesis. The word Vedanta means 'conclusion of the Vedas,' and encompasses the ideas that emerged from, or aligned and reinterpreted, the speculations and enumerations contained in the Upanishads, focusing, with varying emphasis, on devotion, knowledge, and liberation.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: The influence of Vedanta is prominent in the sacred literatures of Hinduism, such as the various Puranas, Samhitas, Agamas and _____ ..
Vedanta.fact: The influence of Vedanta is prominent in the sacred literatures of Hinduism, such as the various Puranas, Samhitas, Agamas and Tantras ..

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: The Upanishads may be regarded as the end of _____ in different senses: They were the last literary products of the Vedic period
Vedanta.fact: Anta (अन्त) — meaning "end." The word Vedanta literally means the end of the Vedas and originally referred to the Upanishads. Vedanta is concerned with the jñānakāṇḍa or knowledge section of the vedas which is called the Upanishads.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: They represent the pinnacle of _____ philosophy
Vedanta.fact: The Upanishads may be regarded as the end of Vedas in different senses: They were the last literary products of the Vedic period. They represent the pinnacle of Vedic philosophy.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers
Vedanta.question: It is also called _____ Mīmāṃsā, which means the "latter enquiry" or "higher enquiry"; and is often contrasted with Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, the "former enquiry" or "primary enquiry"
Vedanta.fact: It is also called Uttara Mīmāṃsā, which means the "latter enquiry" or "higher enquiry"; and is often contrasted with Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, the "former enquiry" or "primary enquiry". Pūrva Mīmāṃsā deals with the karmakāṇḍa or ritualistic section (the Samhita and Brahmanas) in the Vedas while Uttara Mīmāṃsā concerns itself with the deeper questions of the relation between humans and Divine or Absolute reality.

Vedanta.subject: Indian Philosophy & Thinkers

Zwiefalten Abbey.fact: The Abbey of Our Lady of Zwiefalten, more commonly called Zwiefalten Abbey (German: Kloster Zwiefalten, Abtei Zwiefalten or, after 1750, Reichsabtei Zwiefalten) is a former Benedictine monastery situated at Zwiefalten, near Reutlingen, in the German State of Baden-Württemberg.
